divergences.description: The game applies each type-chart row in table order with integer truncation (x5/10 or x20/10 per row, BattleSystem_Divide), so a resisted-then-super-effective dual type (e.g. Fire vs Water/Grass, Ice vs Water/Flying) can lose 1 HP: floor(d/2)*2. Showdown sums effectiveness first and multiplies x2 then /2, so the pair cancels exactly. Game damage <= Showdown by up to 1. Example: Garchomp Flamethrower vs Ludicolo: port/game rolls are even (e.g. 60) where Showdown gives the odd value (61); hand case in damage.test.mjs: 41 -> STAB 61 -> x5/10 = 30 -> x20/10 = 60 (Showdown 61). Also Milotic Ice Beam vs Gyarados.
divergences.impact: Showdown resolves real damage (Constitution II), so battle damage can differ from the cartridge by about 1-3 HP on some rolls; the AI's own damage estimate uses the game formula (sim/damage.mjs).

divergences.description: Game: a Sniper crit sets criticalMul = 3 and multiplies the base damage before the random roll. Showdown: crit x2 before the roll, then Sniper as a chained x1.5 in the final ModifyDamage step after random, STAB and type. Rolls differ by about 1-3 HP in either direction. Example: Aaron's Drapion (Sniper) crit X-Scissor vs Lucian's Alakazam: port [310,314,318,...,366], Showdown [309,312,318,...,366].
divergences.impact: Showdown resolves real damage (Constitution II), so battle damage can differ from the cartridge by about 1-3 HP on some rolls; the AI's own damage estimate uses the game formula (sim/damage.mjs).

divergences.description: Game: Expert Belt = damage*(100+20)/100, floored. Showdown: chainModify([4915,4096]) with 4096-based round-to-nearest. Showdown is 1 HP higher on some rolls. Example: Cynthia's Lucario (Expert Belt) Aura Sphere vs Tyranitar: port 321 vs Showdown 322 on the lowest roll (pre-belt 268: game 32160/100 = 321; Showdown (268*4915+2047)>>12 = 322).
divergences.impact: Showdown resolves real damage (Constitution II), so battle damage can differ from the cartridge by about 1-3 HP on some rolls; the AI's own damage estimate uses the game formula (sim/damage.mjs).

divergences.description: Game applies Filter/Solid Rock (BattleSystem_Divide(d*3,4)) and then Expert Belt (d*120/100) as two separately floored steps. Showdown chains 0.75 and 1.2 into one 4096-based modifier (3686/4096) and rounds once. Showdown 1 HP higher on some rolls. (Filter/Solid Rock alone never diverged: after a x2/x4 the damage is even, where floor and Showdown rounding agree.) Example: Spiritomb (Expert Belt) Shadow Ball vs Lucian's Mr. Mime (Filter): port [80,80,82,...,97], Showdown [81,81,83,...,97].
divergences.impact: Showdown resolves real damage (Constitution II), so battle damage can differ from the cartridge by about 1-3 HP on some rolls; the AI's own damage estimate uses the game formula (sim/damage.mjs).

divergences.description: Game scales move power with floored integer math at each step (e.g. Dry Skin power*125/100). Showdown applies base-power modifiers through chainModify with 4096-based round-to-nearest. Seen on Dry Skin; any other power modifier whose exact result has a fractional part >= ~0.5 can diverge the same way (type items, Muscle Band/Wise Glasses, Iron Fist, Rivalry, Technician stacks) — not observed in the tested cases for those. Example: Flint's Magmortar Flamethrower (power 95) vs Dry Skin Toxicroak: game power 95*125/100 = 118, Showdown (95*5120+2047)>>12 = 119; rolls port [127..151] vs Showdown [129..153].
divergences.impact: Showdown resolves real damage (Constitution II), so battle damage can differ from the cartridge by about 1-3 HP on some rolls; the AI's own damage estimate uses the game formula (sim/damage.mjs).

divergences.description: Game multiplies the raw stat by Choice Band/Specs, Huge Power, Hustle, Guts, Marvel Scale, Soul Dew etc. first, and applies the stat-stage fraction last (inside the damage expression). Showdown applies the stage first (calculateStat) and the Modify(Atk|SpA|Def|SpD) multipliers after, rounded. Diverges when a stage is non-zero (seen with -1 Atk; +1 matched in the tested case). Example: Choice Band Garchomp (Atk 238) at -1 Atk: game floor(238*150/100)=357 -> 357*10/15 = 238; Showdown floor(238/1.5)=158 -> modify(158,1.5) = 237. EQ vs Infernape: port [320,326,...,380] vs Showdown [320,324,...,378].

divergences.description: Resist berries (Occa ... Chilan). Game: a battle subscript halves the final HP change (DivideVarByValue, rounded toward zero, min 1) when HP is updated, after the Focus Sash/Endure clamp; Counter, Mirror Coat and Shell Bell use the full damage; no trigger on substitute hits. Showdown: halves inside the damage calculation (onSourceModifyDamage, chainModify(0.5)), so Counter/Mirror Coat see the halved damage and the order relative to Focus Sash differs.

divergences.description: Opponent Full Restore uses the project pseudo-move `trainerfullrestore`, because Showdown has no bag items. sim/ai/patches.mjs heals in Showdown's beforeTurnCallback and removes its own move action, so it never runs as a move: Taunt, Encore, sleep/freeze/paralysis, confusion, attraction, Truant and Pressure cannot affect it, lastMove is untouched, Sucker Punch fails against it and Heal Block does not stop it, as in the game. Remaining differences: Choice lock (no League mon holds a Choice item), an encored item user facing Sucker Punch, a player Transform on the same turn copying the extra slot, and message order.
divergences.impact: Corrected by sim/ai/patches.mjs + sim/ai/items.mjs (T047). The remaining edge cases listed above do not arise with League parties, apart from the encored-Sucker-Punch case, which is a single-turn ordering difference.

divergences.description: Showdown has no experience. The game layer tracks participation the game's way and computes exp per BtlCmd_CalcExpGain / BattleScript_GetExpTask (trainer x1.5, Lucky Egg x1.5, Exp. Share split, traded x1.5/x1.7; a Build whose source is an NPC trade is traded, language from the trade's FixedMon vs GAME_LANGUAGE). Ordering: the game only flags the payout when the enemy faints and pays at MOVE_END, after the attacker's recoil, the faint loop and Life Orb (and, at end of turn, before each field/mon-condition step), so an attacker KO'd by its own recoil/Life Orb gets nothing. Showdown fires the enemy's Faint before the recoil; sim/exp.mjs therefore queues the award and pays it when the Showdown action returns, or after each residual handler (T072 fix; before it, such an attacker was paid). Remaining approximation: side-condition residuals (Future Sight, Perish Song) are paid per Showdown handler instead of at TurnEnd.

divergences.description: Showdown has no in-game trainer AI. The project runs the decomp's AI scripts in an interpreter (research R6): move choice (TrainerAI_Init/EvalMoves/MainSingles), switch and item choice in TrainerAI_PickCommand order.
divergences.impact: Corrected by the `decomp-ai` opponent policy (T045-T048), now the default. Remaining UNVERIFIED reconstructions from Showdown's log: the AI's knowledge of the player's ability and item, the move that last hit it, and last-move success; Gyro Ball speed values are recomputed per decision. No cartridge comparison has been made. Showdown-mismatch counters (invalidChoice, trappedSwitch, lockMismatch) are reported per run.

divergences.description: Pickup and Honey Gather can give the holder an item after a won battle, trainer battles included (BtlCmd_GenerateEndOfBattleItem). The gauntlet does not model end-of-battle item generation, so these abilities have no effect in simulation.
divergences.impact: Only an item gained between League rooms; it never changes a battle in progress. The ability screen will see a tie for these and keep slot 1 (FR-008c).

divergences.description: The cartridge's battle RNG is a 32-bit LCG (BattleSystem_RandNext); Showdown uses a seeded ChaCha20 (sodium) PRNG, and draws random numbers in a different order and count. Individual battles cannot be reproduced from a cartridge seed.
divergences.impact: None on the estimates: results are win-rate distributions over seeded runs (Constitution IV), reproducible from the project seed, not from the cartridge.

divergences.description: Shift battle style (the game's default). After a turn in which the trainer's active fainted and the player's did not, in a single non-link, non-Frontier battle with a usable replacement on the player's side, the game names the trainer's next Pokemon (chosen by the trainer AI before the prompt, against the player's current active) and offers the player a free switch before it enters; the switch is a normal switch with no move used before the next command selection. Showdown only asks the side whose Pokemon fainted (Set style).

divergences.description: After a Shift switch, the game sends in the player's Pokemon first, then the trainer's, applies entry hazards in that order, and then runs entry abilities by category (weather, Trace, Intimidate, Download, ...) and speed order. Showdown orders the two instant switches by the outgoing Pokemon's speed (seeded tie shuffle) and runs each entering Pokemon's hazards and switch-in abilities after both have entered, in the entering Pokemon's speed order.

divergences.description: Low Kick and Grass Knot power from the target's weight. Game: the first sWeightToPower limit >= weight gives the power (100:20, 250:40, 500:60, 1000:80, 2000:100, else 120), so a weight exactly on a limit takes the LOWER tier. Showdown: thresholds of the form weight >= limit, so a weight exactly on a limit takes the next tier.
